newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks inch down on slow profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks inch down on slow profit-taking.

text.p: Mexican stocks opened marginally down in dead-slow trade on Monday amid what dealers said was light profit-taking and market caution ahead of second quarter reports.
"The bourse is taking a breather after the recent rally and market players are waiting for second quarter earnings, and that's about it," a desk trader said.
The leading IPC share index was down 4.31 points in the opening minutes of trade, or 0.09 percent, at 4,817.31. Trading volume was 603,000 shares.
"We expect a (downward) adjustment later in the day," the trader added.
Financial group Banamex-Accival, one of Mexico's biggest, weighed most on the market and was down five centavos at 20.20 pesos.

Floor traders noted that market heavyweight Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex) reflected what they called "market apathy." Telmex accounted for 70 percent of all shares traded in early dealing and was unchanged at 21.00 pesos. The telecom firm's ADRs were similarly sluggish and off 1/8 at 53-7/16, despite early gains on Wall Street.
The Dow Jones was meanwhile up 15.33 points at 7,937.15. On the broad market, meanwhile, sliders and gainers were evenly balanced at five each, out of a total of 19 stocks traded.
